title: Dataflow Gen2 in Fabric — Microsoft Fabric Tutorial Series
summary: An independent tutorial-site walkthrough of Dataflow Gen2 performance features (Fast Copy, partitioned compute) with a worked cost-optimization example, last verified June 2026.
audience: Data engineers and Fabric capacity owners trying to reduce Dataflow Gen2 execution time and consumption cost on real workloads.
why_it_matters: Provides a concrete, staged cost/performance comparison for common Dataflow Gen2 optimizations that is more actionable than a features list, though the specific numbers are the author's own benchmark and not a Microsoft-published figure.
takeaways: Dataflow Gen2 runs Power Query M transformations on a Spark-based backend, which is why it scales differently than Gen1 dataflows.
Fast Copy skips the Power Query transformation engine for raw ingestion but only supports Parquet and CSV and cannot use VNet or on-premises gateways.
Partitioned Compute can auto-detect Hive-style partition folders and parallelize without hand-written M code.
Combining Fast Copy, a modern evaluator setting, and Partitioned Compute compounded to a large execution-time and cost reduction in the author's own benchmark.
Dataflow Gen2 Classic was retired for new items as of April 2026 per the post.

claims.text: Dataflow Gen2 executes Power Query M transformations on a managed Spark backend rather than the mashup engine used by Gen1 dataflows, which is the underlying reason it can scale to larger data volumes.

Fast Copy bypasses the Power Query transformation engine entirely for raw ingestion, but is limited to Parquet and CSV source formats and explicitly does not support VNet data gateways or on-premises data gateways.

In the author's own benchmark of a 6 GB daily load on an F64 capacity, layering Fast Copy, a modern query evaluator setting, and Partitioned Compute together reduced execution time from roughly 30 minutes to about 1.5 minutes and reduced the estimated cost per run substantially versus the unoptimized baseline; this is the post's own test, not a Microsoft-published benchmark.

Partitioned Compute can automatically detect Hive-style hierarchical partition folder structures (such as year/month partitioning) in ADLS Gen2 and parallelize the dataflow's execution across them without requiring manual M query changes.

Dataflow Gen2 supports an Execute Query API that lets a specific query be run on demand outside the normal scheduled-refresh cycle, useful for triggering transformation logic from an external orchestrator.

Dataflow Gen2 Classic was no longer available for creating new items as of April 2026 per the post, meaning new dataflow work should target the current Dataflow Gen2 experience rather than the classic one.

Dataflow Gen2 items support version control by storing their Power Query logic as plain-text .pq files, which enables normal Git diffing and review workflows through Fabric's Git integration with GitHub or Azure DevOps.
